title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يشارك في أعمال ملتقى المفكرين المسلمين بماليزيا
title_en: The Sheikh Takes Part in the Proceedings of the Forum of Muslim Thinkers in Malaysia
body_ar: يشارك فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى في ملتقى المفكرين المسلمين المنعقد في العاصمة الماليزية كوالارمبور اليوم 30 ابريل 2014 الموافق 1 رجب 1435هـ و قد تحدث فضيلة الشيخ عن موضوع الاستبداد و مخاطر الردة عن الحرية مؤكدا أن القرءان قدم لنا الكثير من التفاصيل عن الاستبداد وطرق تشكله وسبل مواجهته وأن قصة موسى عليه السلام التي تكررت في القرءان كثيرا تكشف مكونات الاستبداد اﻷربعة في كل زمان وكل مكان. وأضاف الشيخ الددو أن مكونات الاستبداد كما نجدها في هذه القصة هي الحاكم المتجبر الذي مثله فرعون والوزير المتملق الذين مثله هامان ورجل الاعمال المحتكر والظالم الذي مثله قارون ورجل الاعلام المزور للواقع والمروج للطغيان. وتابع الشيخ قوله إن الاستبداد يمثل خطرا على دين اﻷمة وأمنها كما أنه يمثل مدخلا للمحتل ونصيرا له وكان الشيخ الددو أول المتحدثين صباح اليوم في ملتقى المفكرين المسلمين بماليزيا الذي يشارك فيه العشرات من العلماء والمفكرين وقادة الرأي في اﻷمة ويتطرق الملتقى لسبل مواجهة اﻷمة للتحديات الراهنة ويستمر مدة يومين باشراف الاتحاد الاسلامي الماليزي.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) is taking part in the Forum of Muslim Thinkers convening in the Malaysian capital, Kuala Lumpur, today, 30 April 2014, corresponding to 1 Rajab 1435 AH.

The Sheikh spoke on the subject of despotism and the dangers of turning back from freedom, affirming that the Qur'an has set out for us a great deal of detail about despotism, the ways in which it takes shape, and the means of confronting it; and that the story of Moses (peace be upon him), repeated many times over in the Qur'an, lays bare the four components of despotism in every time and every place.

Sheikh al-Dedew added that the components of despotism, as we find them in this story, are: the tyrannical ruler, whose likeness was Pharaoh; the fawning minister, whose likeness was Haman; the hoarding and wrongdoing man of business, whose likeness was Korah; and the man of the media who falsifies reality and promotes tyranny.

The Sheikh went on to say that despotism represents a danger to the community's religion and its security, and that it also represents a way in for the occupier, and an ally to him.

Sheikh al-Dedew was the first of the speakers this morning at the Forum of Muslim Thinkers in Malaysia, in which dozens of the community's scholars, thinkers and opinion leaders are taking part. The forum addresses the ways in which the community may confront the challenges of the present, and runs for two days under the auspices of the Malaysian Islamic Union.

flags.arabic: الاستبداد و مخاطر الردة عن الحرية
flags.context: the subject of the Sheikh's talk
options: despotism and the dangers of turning back from freedom
tyranny and the dangers of backsliding from liberty
despotism and the dangers of apostasy from freedom
flags.note: ردة is the word used for apostasy from religion, and using it of freedom is a deliberate rhetorical move: a return to despotism is figured as a reversion of the same kind. 'Turning back' keeps the movement without importing the religious charge into English, where 'apostasy from freedom' would read as a coinage rather than a figure. A reviewer may prefer the stronger third option.

flags.arabic: ورجل الاعلام المزور للواقع والمروج للطغيان
flags.context: the fourth of the four components of despotism
options: the fourth component is given without a Qur'anic counterpart
a name has dropped out of the report
flags.note: The first three components are each matched to a figure from the story of Moses — Pharaoh, Haman, Korah. The fourth, the media man, is given no counterpart. Whether the Sheikh named one and the report dropped it cannot be told from the record. Nothing has been supplied.

flags.arabic: الاستبداد يمثل خطرا على دين اﻷمة وأمنها كما أنه يمثل مدخلا للمحتل ونصيرا له
flags.context: the Sheikh's concluding point as reported
flags.note: EDITORIAL. This record reports the Sheikh delivering a sustained critique of authoritarian rule, naming a hoarding business class and a state-aligned media as constituents of it, and tying despotism to foreign occupation. Rendered faithfully, neither softened nor sharpened. Published in English it is quotable political speech, and carries risk for the Sheikh and for anyone circulating it in some jurisdictions. Whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.
SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): plural relative pronoun where the singular is required, as in the three parallel clauses. Preserved unchanged in body_ar.

translator_notes: A news report of a talk, not a transcript. The Sheikh's positions here are reported in the site's words, not quoted, and the English must not be cited as his wording.
قارون is given as Korah, the form standard in English; the Qur'anic form Qarun is equally usable and the office may prefer it.
The source uses the Arabic Presentation Forms codepoint for ﻷ in several words; preserved as served.
